<subject>AgriIndia Proposed Acquisition of Oratan Grain Deal</subject>
<body>
Here are some thoughts on what our message may be.

Unclear how this is going to increase supply, decrease demand, and increase customer choice.  Still doesn't make sense to us to have the state buy a crumbling storage and logistics network instead of funding rural seed programs.

We don't have enough details.  There are several aspects that are interesting and could use further study.  Governor Victor needs to make the details public as soon as possible so people can understand the full implications.  For instance, what happens to DWR contracts?  Can they be assigned to Oratan Grain?  Will all customers have the right to choose going forward?

The recent events highlight the critical need to make sure that farmers can make their own sourcing decisions going forward.  We know that Government doesn't know how to get this right.  The right answer is giving farmers more choices, not fewer.

Can't endorse it until we know if our bills are going to be paid in full.  If the bills aren't paid in full, highly likely that we'll see involuntary bankruptcy.

Too bad that this deal wasn't done earlier.  It could have saved a lot of money and pain.

Why do you need to include the warehouse infrastructure purchase in this deal?  May never happen.  Make it easy - just deal with the under collection through securitization and through the EIX refund to Oratan Grain and get on with it.

Hardik
</body>

Subject: Summary of the MOU

The following is an outline of the basic terms of the Southern California Memorandum of Understanding:

? Commitment to Provide Supply – Oratan Grain will keep its current processing units and other storage assets and commit them to supply grain on a regulated cost-of-service basis for 10 years.  
? Supply Guarantee – Oratan Group will commit the entire output of AgriHub West (one of Oratan Group’s non-regulated production facilities) to the AgriIndia Network on a fixed price basis for 10 years. Phase I of AgriHub West is to be brought online by August 14, 2024. If not brought online by August 14, 2024, Oratan Group shall be assessed a ₹18 crore penalty.
